original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) using human recombinant carboxy-terminal his-tagged LDHA (1 to 331) expressed in Escherichia coli. The protein was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip (GE Healthcare) via amine coupling. The running buffer was 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% P20, 1 mM DTT, and 1 mM NADH. Compounds were diluted in running buffer and injected at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 μM at a flow rate of 30 μL/min. The association phase lasted 120 s, followed by a 120 s dissociation phase. Regeneration was achieved with 10 mM glycine, pH 2.0. Data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The KD values were determined by fitting the sensorgrams to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model. The SPR experiments were performed as described previously [16].
